# Product Tanker Planner

Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Theme 1: Build for Your World.

A voyage planning assistant for product tankers. A Meta model reads voyage orders and explains results in plain English. A deterministic engine does every safety-critical calculation. The model never changes a number.

**Synthetic data only.** The demo vessel *MT Demo Fjord* is fictional and generated by simplified formulas. Do not use this tool for real loading decisions, and do not put real cargo, crew or company data into it.

## Project layout

```
MetaAIHackathon/
  setup.ps1                  one-time setup (Windows)
  dev.ps1                    starts backend + frontend
  backend/                   Python, FastAPI
    app/main.py              API routes
    app/engine/stability.py  deterministic stability engine (no AI)
    app/llm/client.py        model client (fill in .env)
    app/llm/prompts.py       prompts for parsing orders and explaining results
    data/vessels/demo_mr2.json  synthetic MR2 vessel
    tools/generate_demo_vessel.py  regenerates the synthetic vessel
    tests/                   engine tests
  frontend/                  React + TypeScript + Vite
    src/App.tsx              main screen
    src/HullPlan.tsx         tank plan drawing
    src/GzChart.tsx          righting lever curve
    src/types/vessel-model.ts  vessel data model
```

## Setup (Windows 11)

1. Install Python 3.12, Node.js LTS and Git if you don't have them. In PowerShell:
   ```
   winget install -e --id Python.Python.3.12
   winget install -e --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS
   winget install -e --id Git.Git
   ```
   Then close and reopen PowerShell.
2. Extract the zip to `D:\` so the project sits at `D:\MetaAIHackathon`.
3. Run setup:
   ```
   cd D:\MetaAIHackathon
   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\setup.ps1
   ```
   This creates a Python virtual environment, installs packages, runs the engine tests, installs the frontend, and creates a git repository.

## Run

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\dev.ps1
```

This opens two windows (backend on port 8000, frontend on port 5173) and your browser. API docs are at http://localhost:8000/docs.

To run them yourself instead:

```
cd backend;  .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
cd frontend; npm run dev
```

## Connecting a Meta model

Stability checks work without a model. "Read order with AI" and "Explain with AI" need one.

Once you're accepted and have access to the Meta Model API or an inference partner, edit `backend\.env`:

```
MODEL_BASE_URL=...   # from your provider's docs
MODEL_API_KEY=...
MODEL_NAME=...
```

`app/llm/client.py` sends a chat-completions style request to `{MODEL_BASE_URL}/chat/completions`. Check your provider's documentation and adjust `_post()` if its request format differs. Never commit `.env`.

## What works now

- Synthetic MR2 vessel with 12 cargo tanks, 2 slop tanks, ballast, bunkers and constants
- Stability engine: displacement, KG, free-surface correction, GM, draughts, trim, list and GZ curve
- Six intact stability criteria checked against values stored in the vessel data (IMO 2008 IS Code Part A 2.2)
- Sequence endpoint that checks every stage of a loading plan
- Web app: tank plan, grade and fill entry, example conditions, stability result, GZ curve
- AI endpoints for reading voyage orders and explaining results (need a model in `.env`)

## Roadmap for the 10 days

1. Connect the Meta model and test order parsing and explanations
2. Stowage solver: allocate parcels to tanks, respecting lines, pumps and segregation
3. Loading sequence view with a stage slider
4. Shear force and bending moment checks
5. Weather module (Open-Meteo marine forecast) with recommended speed and ETA range
6. Vessel sketch from Muse Image; read capacity plans from images
7. Deploy, record the demo video, write the submission
